Our exciting Partnership opportunity in Sherwood could be for you!
We’re on the lookout for a driven and entrepreneurial vet ready to take the next big step in their career by becoming a practice owner.
As a Medivet Partner, you won’t just work in a practice, you will own it, shaping its future while receiving full support from our expert team. You’ll be our local partner, bringing your vision to life with the autonomy to run your clinic your way, backed by Medivet’s operational and strategic support.
The clinic
Medivet Sherwood is a thriving, well-established practice in the heart of Sherwood Housed in a spacious practice which is equipped with three consult rooms, theatre, dental facilities including dental x-ray, that handles a varied caseload of medical and surgical cases.
You’ll be joining a dedicated and compassionate team who are proud of their reputation for going the extra mile for clients and their pets. Why Medivet Partnership?
Medivet’s Partnership model gives you the chance to own your future without having to do it all yourself. It’s a supported, financially rewarding route to ownership—with a low barrier to entry and a strong return over time.
With us, you’ll benefit from:
•  A low initial investment - we handle the heavy lifting
• Monthly profit share from your clinic’s performance
• A guaranteed exit payment when you decide to step away
• Full operational support - from HR and payroll to marketing and health and safety
• A connected community of 150+ Partners to learn from and grow with
You’ll have the freedom to lead, with the backing to succeed.
Your Next Chapter Starts Here
At Medivet Sherwood, you’ll have the chance to:
• Take ownership of an established, well-located clinic
• Build and develop a team aligned with your values
• Deliver outstanding care to a community that trusts you
• Shape the business your way, with Medivet’s support every step of the journey
Start something that’s truly yours - with Medivet by your side.
Pay range and compensation package
When it comes to financial rewards, Partnership offers double the opportunity:
• Uncapped profit share from day one – your profit share will increase as the clinic grows, however you can expect to earn more than an employed vet over your time in the Partnership.
• Guaranteed share buyback on exit – ensuring long-term financial security and peace of mind.
​If you're looking for both professional fulfilment and future stability, Partnership could be the perfect move for you.
Equal Opportunity Statement
We also believe in empowering vets to take ownership of their careers, which is why the Partner community is at the heart of what we do, provide exceptional personalised care for pets.

Ownership from Day One

Full Support

Join our community

quilter.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/external-c.description_excerpt:
About the Business
Quilter plc is a leading wealth management business, helping to enable brighter financial futures for every generation.
Quilter oversees £157.4 billion in customer investments (as of August 2026). It has an adviser and customer offering spanning financial advice, investment platforms, multi-asset investment solutions, and discretionary fund management. The business is comprised of two segments: Affluent and High Net Worth.
Affluent encompasses the financial planning business, Quilter Financial Planning, the Quilter Investment Platform and Quilter Investors, the multi-asset investment solutions business.
High Net Worth includes the discretionary fund management business, Quilter Cheviot, together with Quilter Cheviot Financial Planning – offering a highly personalised service to private clients, charities, trustees, and professional partners. Quilter Cheviot has presence throughout the UK, Ireland and Channel Islands.
At Quilter we never stand still. Our foundations are rooted in our extraordinary expertise, which is trusted by hundreds of thousands of customers, but we have great ambitions to stay one step ahead and make an even greater difference to the people and communities we serve, including our colleagues.
Our business is transforming, continually modernising, and becoming even more customer centric. So, if you want to be bold in the pursuit of your ambitions, bring new ideas, and challenge and evolve what we do, it’s the perfect time to join us!
About the Role
Level: 4
Department: HR
Location: Southampton, United Kingdom (With travel to London and other Quilter offices when required)
Contract Type: Permanent
Regulated/Non-Regulated: Non-Regulated
Quilter is reshaping how colleagues build the skills they need to perform, grow and deliver for customers. As Digital Learning Experience Lead, you will help create that shift by reinventing the learning experience, making development easier to access, more relevant to people’s work and more effective at building capability. You will be the business lead for learning experience, adoption, digital content and learning technology requirements, working in partnership with HR Information & Systems, which retains technical ownership of the underlying platforms.
You will turn business priorities and user needs into simple, engaging learning journeys, using Workday Learning powered by Sana and emerging technologies as enablers. You will lead the learning experience, content and adoption activity required to move away from legacy learning technology. Working alongside HR Information & Systems and the wider People team, you will also help develop Workday Skills Cloud through initial pilots and create the insight, content and experiences needed to accelerate upskilling across high-priority areas aligned to Quilter’s strategic delivery.
This is a hands-on opportunity to create, experiment and make a visible organisational impact. You will combine technology, user experience, learning design, e-learning authoring and data to re-engineer how learning is created, discovered and used.
Your key areas of focus will include:
Reinvent the learning experience
• Put colleagues and their journeys at the centre, creating simple, inclusive and engaging experiences that make priority skills, role-based, mandatory, onboarding and culture-aligned learning easier to access and apply.
• Shape how Workday Learning powered by Sana and emerging technologies are used to make learning easier to find, access and apply, translating colleague insight into experience and content improvements.
• Create high-quality e-learning using Articulate, Elucidat and Sana, and enable subject matter experts to create effective content through practical guidance, templates and support.
Build skills for the future
• Lead the learning experience and business implementation of Workday Skills Cloud pilots, partnering with HR Information & Systems on technology configuration and delivery.
• Work with pilot areas Talent, People and HR Information & Systems to connect priority skills to relevant learning, test the colleague experience and use evidence to shape recommendations for wider rollout.
• Explore AI-enabled learning approaches that can improve personalisation, content creation and capability building.
Shape and embed the digital learning experience
• Act as the Learning subject matter expert for Workday Learning powered by Sana and related learning technologies, translating business and colleague needs into clear requirements and recommendations.
• Lead the evolution of the colleague learning experience across Workday Learning powered by Sana, including the content, user journeys, communications and adoption required to move successfully away from legacy learning technology.
• Partner with HR Information & Systems to define learning requirements and ensure technical changes deliver the intended learning and colleague experience.
• Simplify mandatory and role-based learning, strengthening SME ownership while improving relevance, experience and efficiency.
• Work with HR Information & Systems who will retain accountability for system governance, configuration, release management, technical testing, technical controls and the overall HR technology roadmap.
Use insight to create impact
• Build a clear view of participation, engagement, learner experience, skills and business impact through learning data and feedback.
• Use insight to challenge existing approaches, prioritise investment and identify opportunities for reinvention.
• Drive business adoption of learning technologies by helping colleagues, managers and content owners understand and use the learning ecosystem effectively.
Enable cultural and organisational change
• Create the digital learning experiences that support meaningful shifts in culture, leadership, ways of working and organisational capability.
• Lead the digital learning experience for priority culture, leadership and capability programmes, from user journey and content design through to adoption, evaluation and improvement.
• Partner across Culture and Learning, Talent, People, the business and Communications to turn strategic priorities into experiences that change how people work.
About You
You are a digital learning experience specialist with strong expertise in learning platforms, user experience and user journey design. You understand how people interact with technology and can turn business and colleague needs into clear requirements and simple, intuitive and engaging learning experiences. You combine strategic thinking with hands-on capability, using technology, content and insight to reimagine how learning is created, discovered and used across Quilter.
You will use your expertise and credibility to challenge how learning works today, bring people with you and turn ideas into experiences that colleagues value and use. You are curious, practical and comfortable experimenting, learning quickly and making bold improvements…

Involved in model and MI development as well as use of the capital model throughout the business.  Opportunities to liaise and form close working relationships with the wider business.  Communication and presentation of analysis and results to key internal (incl. senior management) and external stakeholders (incl. the parent company and regulator).

Assist in the production and delivery of regulatory and economic capital requirements (SCR / ECA / Standard Formula) for all Chaucer managed syndicates;
•
Run capital models to understand capital implications of business decisions as required;

Are you an RF & Electronics Engineer looking for a new challenge in a production-facing design support role? Do you enjoy problem solving and collaboration where no two days are the same? Our team of Production Support Engineers is expanding and we are looking for a motivated & experienced individual to undertake a production support lead role focused on transceiver-based datalink products that are used within industry leading missile systems.
Salary: £54-61K depending on experience
Dynamic (hybrid) working: 4-5 days per week on-site due to workload classification
Security Clearance: British Citizen or a Dual UK national with British citizenship
Restrictions and/or limitations relating to nationality and/or rights to work may apply. As a minimum and after offer stage, all successful candidates will need to undergo HMG Basic Personnel Security Standard checks (BPSS), which are managed by the MBDA Personnel Security Team.
What we can offer you:
• Company bonus: Up to £2,500 (based on company performance and will vary year to year
• Pension: maximum total (employer and employee) contribution of up to 14%
• Overtime: opportunity for paid overtime
• Flexi Leave: Up to 15 additional days
• Flexible working: We welcome applicants who are looking for flexible working arrangements
• Enhanced parental leave: offers up to 26 weeks for maternity, adoption and shared parental leave -enhancements are available for paternity leave, neonatal leave and fertility testing and treatments
• Facilities: Fantastic site facilities including subsidised meals, free car parking and much more…
The opportunity:
We have a fantastic opportunity for an RF & Electronics Engineer to play a leading role in the support of Datalink production activities at our state of the art manufacturing facility in Bolton.
Reporting to the Production Design Support delivery team leader, as the appointed Production Support Lead for our Datalink products in Bolton you will mainly interface between the Design Authority in Stevenage and the various Manufacturing teams in Bolton working on products in series production and under development. As a highly motivated, driven & experienced engineer you will be required to respond to any issues raised by Manufacturing and/or Design teams that may affect our ability to deliver product with a strong emphasis on raising & maintaining high yield rates.
You will be expected to demonstrate hands-on, face to face production support in many forms such as devising and conducting factory-based trials & proving activities, generating formal evidence and effective collaboration with various Engineering & Operations Managers, Quality Assurance, Supply Chain & Design Authorities when resolving unforeseen production issues. You will be required to generate an in-depth understanding our Datalink Products & associated Test Equipment designs including production test requirements in order to quickly & effectively distinguish the correct root cause of the issue(s) and the subsequent resolution process. You will also be required to act as a key stakeholder & peer reviewer for new, emerging Datalink designs focusing on providing feedback in relation to Design for Test and Design for Manufacture based upon experience & problems raised by Manufacturing.
In addition, you will be required to provide RF technical leadership & guidance to other support engineers in the team. Drawing on your experiences you will work autonomously in isolation or within small, focused investigation teams who will be looking to you for guidance and support in relation to RF components, circuits, systems, testing & analysis. Where minor revisions to product designs are required, you will act as the main contact interfacing between the Design Authority and Manufacturing, fulfilling and overseeing any practical evidence gathering activities including the generation of requirement documentation.
The role offers the successful candidate a true engineering challenge in their core discipline(s), whilst providing scope for personal growth and development in other areas of electronics while working on some of the most exciting missile & platform programmes in defence.
Working within Production Design support team is a challenging but highly rewarding role as you not only see designs coming to life in the manufacturing environment but you can help to shape the design of these products to deliver support to our customers.
What we're looking for from you:
• Proven practical RF design, testing & Fault Finding of RF circuits down to component level across a wide frequency range including Low Noise Amplifiers (LNA’s), High Power Amplifiers (HPA’s), filters & attenuators, local oscillators, synthesisers, modulator design etc.
• Experience using RF design tools ( eg Microwave Office), including layout.
• Significant RF Test & Measurement experience including fault finding, RF calibration and measurement uncertainty is highly desirable and the proficient use of RF test equipment including Vector Network Analysers (VNA’s), Spectrum Analysers, Oscilloscopes & Power Meters etc.
• Experience in RF production test requirements and evaluation of correct implementation via test equipment
• Excellent practical skills including soldering, designing and building development boards for proving activities etc.
• Good knowledge of digital, analogue and power supply design
• Fully conversant with manufacturing techniques and capabilities, including design for manufacture and test.
• Strong communicator with excellent presentation and report writing skills. Able to communicate clearly any problems, solutions or results to various teams at all levels including Design Authorities, customers & Suppliers. Able to provide demonstrations and training to other support engineers.
Our company: Peace is not a given, Freedom is not a given, Sovereignty is not a given
MBDA is a leading defence organisation.  We are proud of the role we play in supporting the Armed Forces who protect our nations. We partner with governments to work together towards a common goal, defending our freedom.
We are proud of our employee-led networks, examples include: Gender Equality, Pride, Menopause Matters, Parents and Carers, Armed Forces, Ethnic Diversity, Neurodiversity, Disability and more…

PerkinElmer is seeking an Operations Product Manager - UV to support the ongoing execution of the product portfolio for an assigned analytical instrument product line. The Operations Product Manager is a junior-to-mid-career product management role, working under the direction of the Strategic PM or VP Product Line. • Support NPI launches with operational readiness tasks: SAP setup, price book entry, configuration guide development, and sales team resource publication

Architect secure data integration using batch, streaming, APIs, change data capture and event-driven patterns.

Mentor data engineers and architects and promote reusable platform capabilities and engineering standards.

Significant experience as a Data Architect, Lead Data Architect, Principal Data Engineer or comparable senior technical leader.

Proven ownership of modern data platforms or data products from architecture through production delivery and operation.

Strong experience in data privacy and security, including data masking, anonymisation, tokenisation or comparable privacy-preserving patterns for sensitive or customer data.

Strong data-modelling expertise across conceptual, logical, physical, dimensional and canonical models.

Experience with batch and real-time integration, including APIs, CDC, streaming or event-driven pipelines.

A strong data-engineering or software-development foundation using Python, SQL, Scala, Java and/or Spark.

Deep experience with Azure data services. AWS experience is advantageous as the platform expands.

PS attach across EMEA. You are the commercial owner of services from RFP and initial deal scoping through close and into renewal.

• Strong C/C++ systems programming skills and expertise in Windows kernel drivers, WinDbg/KD, ETW/WPP, crash dump analysis, and profiling; WFP/NDIS experience or willingness to develop expertise in these areas.

• AI-assisted engineering experience is mandatory, including practical use of AI for development, debugging, code analysis, investigation, and technical research.
• Demonstrated ability to take technical ownership, lead complex investigations, coordinate work across teams, and share technical expertise

About Vantage
Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.
Product Department
The Product team at Vantage defines and stewards our global product platform: the customer outcomes we aim to deliver, the standards and reference approaches that make delivery repeatable, and the closed-loop learning that turns each deployment into an upgrade for the next. We do this in partnership with Engineering, Delivery, Operations, Procurement, Sustainability, Sales, Site Selection, and Business Development, aligning priorities and trade-offs while preserving clear functional ownership for design execution, construction delivery, and site operations.
Position Overview
Vantage is building a repeatable, product-led approach to delivering hyperscale infrastructure and operating data centers on a global scale. We are hiring a Senior Manager, Product Performance Benchmarking to establish and evolve the product performance benchmarking capability at the heart of that approach. The benchmarking engine is the governed reference for our products across the full lifecycle, regions, and customer configurations, and will sit behind pricing, RFP responses, and executive reporting for a growing global portfolio.
It evaluates the expected schedule, cost, and sustainability of our products across design, delivery, and operations: how long they should take to build, and what they should cost to build and to run.
This is a senior individual contributor role expected to grow into team leadership for someone who combines deep benchmarking, estimating, preconstruction, and project controls experience with the commercial judgement to lead methodology, challenge conventions, and turn data into decisions. You will define what the benchmark should answer, how it is governed, how it is used in decisions, and how internal and external inputs become a durable capability.
What You Will Own
You will build the product performance intelligence capability behind Vantage’s global data center platform. This is not a reporting role. It is a chance to define how one of the fastest-scaling infrastructure companies measures cost, schedule, sustainability, lifecycle performance, and value realization across regions, product configurations, and customer requirements.
The benchmark you build will shape real decisions: how products are configured, how products translate into cost, schedule, and sustainability impacts, how trade-offs are made, where performance is improving, and where the business needs to change. You will work at the intersection of Product, Engineering, Delivery, Operations, Procurement, Sustainability, and Analytics, with visibility to senior leaders and direct influence over how Vantage becomes more repeatable, data-driven, and product-led.
What You Will Do
•
Define the governed benchmarking methodology, baseline assumptions, performance measures, and usage rules Vantage applies globally to configure, cost, schedule, approve, manage, and measure project performance across Product, Engineering, Delivery, Operations, and Sustainability.
•
Own the benchmark roadmap across platform, product, regional baselines, configurations, and future product extensions.
•
Translate Product, Procurement, Preconstruction, Project Controls, and Sustainability requirements into benchmark scope.
•
Lead consultant engagement, reviewing methodology, assumptions, confidence bands, and deliverables.
•
Own the WBS/CBS and schedule structure from a product, business-adoption, and use perspective.
•
Govern baseline, regional variant, configuration bridge, and factor-pack logic.
•
Partner with key stakeholders to incorporate market intelligence, supplier input, and realized cost factors into benchmark updates where appropriate.
•
Define target audiences, provide business interpretation, and set reporting requirements for benchmark outputs to senior stakeholders, while partnering with analytics roles on dashboard build and data automation.
•
Decide when benchmark outputs are fit for use in RFPs, ROM business cases, customer discussions, product decisions, and executive reporting.
•
Own what decisions the benchmark enables and state clearly where confidence is insufficient.
What Success Looks Like
•
A governed product performance benchmark model exists that connects capital cost, schedule, sustainability and operational cost (energy, efficiency, maintainability) into a single governed reference with explicit methodology, confidence bands, and stated limits.
•
Standardized KPIs and performance criteria are set, with the ability to reliably compare projects across approved variants, regions, and product versions from pre-construction through operations.
•
Benchmark outputs are used in real decisions — RFPs, ROM business cases, customer discussions, product trade-offs, and executive reporting — under clear fitness-for-use rules.
•
The WBS/CBS and schedule structures are adopted by Product, Procurement, Preconstruction, Project Controls, and Sustainability, and held under company change control.
•
Baseline, regional variant, configuration bridge, and factor-pack logic is coherent and current, with refresh cycles running on a disciplined cadence.
•
Benchmarking exists as a durable internal capability that gets better with data from each delivery project. Results inform enhancements to products, variants, and project delivery to continuously improve.
•
Methodology, models, and refresh are owned in-house, with external inputs from consultants, market data, and suppliers integrated deliberately rather than relied upon by default.
•
Senior stakeholders receive interpretation, not just numbers: what moved, why, and what decision it supports.
What We Are Looking For
•
Benchmarking and cost intelligence: 8–12 years in cost management, quantity surveying, preconstruction, owner’s representative, project controls, infrastructure benchmarking, or equivalent capital-project performance role. Exceptional candidates with fewer years of experience may be considered.
•
Capital project modeling: Demonstrated experience building or governing cost, schedule, or TCO models for complex capital programs, including unit rates, quantities, escalation, regional factors, configuration deltas, and confidence ranges.
•
Lifecycle performance orientation: Ability to connect capital cost, schedule, energy, operational cost, maintainability, and sustainability factors into a decision-ready view of product performance.
•
Continuous learning: Experience comparing benchmarks to actual delivery outcomes and translating variance into actionable recommendations for design, procurement, delivery, or product roadmap…

Purpose of the role
The way that academic research is being communicated to audiences around the globe is changing rapidly. Increasingly, research data can be consumed at scale through AI tools and machine intelligence, creating a moment of transition in research communication, and an opportunity to shape how millions discover, trust, and apply research, accelerating the translation of insight into real‑world impact faster than before.
The purpose of this role is to turn Springer Nature’s traffic, usage and discovery data into the signals and evidence the team relies on to maximise the value of our content across the web, navigating this transition. This role sits at the intersection of content discoverability, content protection and data intelligence.
You will help the organisation understand how Springer Nature content is being discovered, accessed and used across search engines, academic discovery services, AI-powered tools, content aggregation platforms and other external channels. At the same time, you will identify and measure inappropriate access, automated scraping and content extraction activities to ensure discoverability is achieved without undermining platform traffic, entitlements or commercial value.
You will own the analytical foundations of both disciplines: identifying and measuring the signals that indicate successful discovery, as well as those that indicate abuse. Working closely with product, platform, analytics and security teams, you will provide the evidence needed to shape strategy, prioritise interventions and measure outcomes.
Key Responsibilities
Content Discoverability & External Platform Analytics
• Analyse how Springer Nature content is discovered across external channels, including search engines, scholarly discovery services, library platforms, aggregators, citation networks, AI-powered discovery tools and emerging content platforms
• Develop and maintain a framework of discoverability metrics, signals and KPIs to measure the effectiveness of content distribution and discovery strategies
• Identify the external signals that indicate successful content discovery, engagement and conversion back to Springer Nature properties

Role summary
The Financial Crime and Sanctions Analyst is a junior-level, second-line role in the Financial Crime and Sanctions (FCS) Team, part of the firm's Legal Department. The role supports the day-to-day implementation of the firm's financial crime and sanctions controls, with a particular focus on client due diligence and reverifications, ongoing monitoring of clients and matters, sanctions monitoring, and gifts and hospitality, as well as support for the firm's remediation project.
You will be at the forefront of compliance in a fast-paced, global environment and will have the opportunity to work on challenging and engaging matters. The focus of this role will be analysing the financial crime, sanctions and reputational risks of existing clients, identifying and gathering client due diligence materials, and escalating key issues to more senior members of the FCS Team.
The role will also involve supporting the FCS Team with quality control (including recording data and analysing trends), regulatory reporting, internal and regulatory audits, and other risk management and compliance projects, such as the implementation of new systems and tools.
Location Overview: Manchester
The Freshfields Global Centre provides both business and legal services to the firm. Our services are delivered in a way which supports the global nature of our firm and our clients, enables our fee earners to deliver exceptional service to our clients and to do that in a way which is efficient and effective.
Function Overview: Legal Department
This department, made up of both qualified lawyers and non-lawyers, exists to manage the firm's risk exposure and to provide advice to the partners on a range of legal and compliance issues. The Financial Crime and Sanctions Analyst will be a member of the global Financial Crime and Sanctions (FCS) Team in the Legal Department. The FCS Team provides advice to the firm on compliance with financial crime and sanctions legislation and gives guidance on reputational risk matters.
Key responsibilities and deliverables
1) Client reverifications and backlog reduction (AML compliance)
• Facilitating the ongoing monitoring process in coordination with partners and fee earners, particularly in the collection and analysis of due diligence material and records for client reverification purposes.
• Driving down the existing client reverification backlog by working through outstanding reverifications in line with agreed priorities and timescales, and tracking and reporting progress to the FCS Team.
2) Ongoing monitoring of clients and matters (AML compliance)
• Providing support and assistance to the FCS Team principally on client due diligence matters.
• Reviewing records, conducting research, screening for PEPs, sanctions, and adverse media, and reputational risk analysis for existing clients with a view to keeping documentation and information for client risk assessments up-to-date and to agreed standards appropriate for review by internal and external stakeholders such as internal audit and regulators.
• Supporting the ongoing monitoring of high-risk clients and matters in coordination with partners and fee earners, including checking that enhanced due diligence and clearance conditions have been applied and documented, and escalating any new or increased financial crime risks to more senior members of the FCS Team.
3) Sanctions monitoring (sanctions compliance)

• Actively executing high-volume, structured CDD and AML remediation projects to ensure client files are brought up to the required regulatory standard within designated project timelines.
• Supporting the delivery of targeted client file review programs, actively managing down backlogs of periodic reviews, and ensuring consistent application of the firm's risk-rating methodology.
• Working efficiently under structured project timelines and meeting defined volume and quality targets to help the firm meet its regulatory and operational commitments.

At Nuffield Health, everything we give our patients, members and customers starts with our people. Your passion, your expertise and your drive to make a difference enable us to deliver exceptional connected healthcare and fitness experiences.
We're looking for an experienced Senior Data Engineer to join our Data Engineering team, responsible for making data available and trusted across the whole of Nuffield Health. This is a role with real ownership: you'll own a functional area of our data platform, lead delivery initiatives and line manage engineers, setting the standards, patterns and direction that the wider team follows.
Our Data Engineering team operates a distributed leadership model. Each Senior Data Engineer owns a defined functional area, such as ingestion and integration, incident management and observability, governance, security and cost management, or CI/CD and DevOps, and is accountable for the standards and resilience of that area so that nothing depends on a single person. Seniors lead delivery initiatives and line manage engineers, with the Lead Data Engineer retaining overall technical direction and the roadmap. You'll work with industry-leading technologies including Snowflake, dbt, Azure Data Factory, Talend, SQL Server, New Relic and Terraform.
Could you play a key role in that?
As our Senior Data Engineer, you'll:
• Own a defined functional area of the data platform, setting the standards, patterns and tooling the team follows within it and acting as the first point of contact for questions in that area.
• Avoid becoming a single point of dependency by documenting your work and helping other engineers develop the knowledge and skills needed to support your area, treating knowledge transfer as an ongoing obligation rather than a one-off handover.
• Lead delivery initiatives end to end, planning, resourcing and delivering against agreed constraints in collaboration with Product Owners, Delivery Managers, architects and third-party suppliers.
• Line manage engineers, including objectives, development plans and reviews, and line manage external or temporary resource aligned to your initiatives for their duration.
• Design, build and operate robust ingestion, integration and transformation solutions on Snowflake, dbt and Azure, in line with Nuffield Health's enterprise architecture and data engineering standards.
• Ensure solutions are operationally ready, observable and supportable, and contribute to incident and problem management as part of the team's service management approach.
• Coach mid-level engineers to take ownership of epics and smaller initiatives within their squad, growing the next generation of leaders in the team.
• Contribute to the team's technical roadmap, BAU planning and engineering maturity, including documentation, code quality, branching and testing standards.
• Escalate cross-cutting risks, dependencies and unassigned questions to the Lead Data Engineer, and communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
To succeed as Senior Data Engineer, you'll bring:
• Substantial hands-on data engineering experience across integration, data modelling and data warehousing, with excellent SQL skills.
• Experience with ETL/ELT tools (e.g. Talend, Azure Data Factory, dbt) and database platforms (e.g. MS SQL Server, Snowflake, Azure SQL Database), including developing integration solutions using APIs, files and databases.
• Experience with performance tuning, data migration strategies (on premise and cloud) and relational database design, particularly in support of business intelligence.
• Experience setting and upholding engineering standards, and taking ownership of quality and outcomes for a technical area.
• Experience leading the delivery of a project or initiative, working with Product Owners, Delivery Managers, architects and third-party suppliers to manage scope, dependencies and risk.
• Line management or mentoring experience, or a clear appetite to develop it with structured support.
• Excellent communication skills, including documenting technical design proposals and translating complex technical concepts for technical and non-technical audiences.
Desirable:
• Observability and incident management tooling, such as New Relic and ServiceNow.
• CI/CD, DevOps and infrastructure as code, such as Terraform and Azure DevOps.
• Data governance and security: data masking, GDPR, access auditing, PII handling, role-based access and cloud cost management.
• Experience in healthcare or another regulated environment.
We will provide:
• A wide variety of interesting and challenging work that involves most of Nuffield Health's systems, working with key stakeholders such as data analysts, data scientists and business intelligence teams.
• Genuine ownership of a functional area and the initiatives you lead, within a community of data engineers where your opinions shape the standards and practices we adopt.
• A structured path into technical leadership and people management: training pathways, shadowing and reverse shadowing, a Seniors peer group, and regular reviews with the Lead Data Engineer.
• Opportunities to learn and develop your career through apprenticeships, self-learning, mentoring and training courses, with progression encouraged both within the team and across Nuffield Health.
• An environment that allows you to perform at your best, working collaboratively with colleagues who are focused on improving the health of our nation and making a real difference to people's everyday lives.

Job Description:
What you'll do as a Senior Stress Engineer:
Mechanical Engineering is a fundamental element of all our products.
Your role as a Senior Stress Engineer will be primarily to support product designs that are in-service or being developed for customers by providing the necessary structural verification that demonstrates compliance against customer and or regulatory specifications. You will communicate key aspects of results and findings to project integrated teams and the company airworthiness authority and technically advise on all aspects of stress engineering activities. It will involve working with multi-discipline project teams, interfacing with customers (internal and external) and liaising closely with engineers from many other disciplines.
Typically, you will:
• Assess mechanical designs for strength, durability (fatigue), performance and safety against regulatory and customer requirements through application of appropriate methodologies i.e. finite element techniques and/or classical hand calculations.
• Provide guidance on structural design improvements relating to component sustainability and manufacturing considerations.
• Provide recommendations on component or sub assembly optimisation i.e. mass reduction, reduced part count etc.
• Support the selection of manufacturing technologies and materials based on a sound understanding of mechanical engineering principles e.g. statics, dynamics (vibration and shock), strength of materials and failure mechanisms.
• Support all structural aspects of product development from concept design through to test and certification.
What we need from you:
• The candidate should have a degree in Mechanical or Aeronautical Engineering with post-graduate experience in stress & vibration engineering.
• Professional recognition as a Chartered Engineer or proven associated competencies is desirable.
• It is advantageous for the candidate to have experience in the design, development and test of electronics packaging and/or aerospace systems equipment.
• A proven knowledge of structural analysis and previous experience in developing equipment for extreme operating environments to RTCA DO160 and MIL-STD-810 mechanical requirements.
• The candidate will be competent in the use of Finite Element Analysis (FEA), preferably Siemens Simcenter & Nastran and be competent in the fundamentals of load balancing i.e. free-body diagrams and application of classical hand calculations using empirical methods in lieu of FEA or in validation of FEA results.
• Experience of environmental testing methods (shock, vibration, acceleration) and post-processing of test results for design verification is highly desirable.
• Verbal and written communication skills are essential in this role as there will be a high level of interaction with both internal and external customers.

Partnering with the global auction community to maximise efficiency, combining our human experience with technology-led solutions.

The Role
We're looking for an enthusiastic, self-motivated Business Development Executive to join our growing commercial team.
This is a true new business sales role, ideal for someone who enjoys identifying opportunities, opening doors and winning new customers.
You'll be responsible for developing new business across the UK and Ireland, promoting our Auctionmarts platform and Auctionmarts Hub software alongside our payments platform to auctioneers and businesses operating within agriculture, livestock, plant and machinery, while helping us expand into wider commercial markets including:
• Plant & Machinery
• Commercial Auctions
• Dispersal Sales
• Asset Disposal
• Industrial Auctions
• Construction
• Groundcare
• Forestry

• Report regularly on pipeline development and sales performance.

• Loves meeting new people and building relationships.
• Is naturally curious and enjoys understanding customers' businesses.

• Enjoys working in a fast-moving technology business.
• Has enthusiasm for agriculture, machinery, auctions or rural industries.
• Takes pride in delivering an excellent customer experience.
• Is excited by innovation, AI and the opportunity to sell market-leading technology.
What We Offer

• Company car or car allowance.
• Pension scheme.
• Laptop and mobile phone.
• Ongoing product and sales training.
• Flexible remote working.
• Opportunity to work with market-leading software used by some of the UK's most respected auction businesses.

• The opportunity to help shape the future of digital auctions through innovative software and AI-powered solutions.

Newline’s Vision is to be the global auction community’s most trusted, transformative auction platform. Continuously evolving, proven at scale and the benchmark by which others are measured.
Newline has been the market leader in auction software for decades. Our reputation has been built through innovation, trusted partnerships and delivering technology that genuinely helps our customers succeed.
As we continue to invest in AI, cloud technologies and new digital services, there's never been a more exciting time to join us. You'll be selling proven products with an outstanding reputation while helping customers embrace the next generation of auction technology.

Job Description
DMPK - Industrial Placement 12 Months
Oxford, UK
Vertex is a global biotechnology company that aims to discover, develop and commercialize innovative new medicines so people with serious diseases can lead better lives. Founded in 1989 in Cambridge, MA, Vertex today has research and development sites and commercial offices around the world in the United States, Canada, Europe and Australia.
Drug Metabolism and Pharmacokinetics (DMPK) is a multidisciplinary group within Vertex.  DMPK plays a critical role in the prediction of human pharmacokinetic profiles in order to determine whether candidate molecules are suitable to progress to clinical development.  DMPK provides support from early discovery to late-development programs.
We are recruiting for an Industrial placement student in the DMPK Department, at our research facility in Oxfordshire, as part of our wider intern intake for the year.
Main Duties & Objectives
The research site is a dynamic, fast-paced environment, where you will be embedded within research teams working on any one of several diseases. You will be working in a close-knit, multidisciplinary team of scientists, located in our research laboratories, where you can expect to gain a broad understanding of the drug discovery process. As part of your time here you can expect to gain experience in DMPK in-vitro assays and their application to prediction of pharmacokinetics, drug metabolism and enzymology and assay development and optimization.
During your Industrial Placement you will get the opportunity to learn about our industry from a hands-on perspective. You will be working closely with and learning from some of the brightest people in the industry. Students can expect to be challenged by their work, connect with other students, and feel valued by the Vertex community.
Person Specification

• Passion for scientific discovery and experimentation
• Desire to develop scientific and laboratory skills

Working with stakeholders across multiple business areas and countries, you'll provide expert guidance on Workday capabilities, challenge existing ways of working and identify opportunities to improve processes, increase automation and enhance the employee experience..

• Manage and resolve Workday incidents, service requests and change requests in line with agreed service levels.

• Configure and maintain reports and dashboards to provide meaningful people insights.

• Stay connected with the wider Workday community, bringing new ideas, innovations and best practice into Arriva.

You'll be someone who enjoys partnering with stakeholders, solving problems and driving continuous improvement through technology.

• Strong communication, facilitation and relationship-building skills.
• Experience working within complex, multinational organisations.

Desirable Experience

• Experience with Workday reporting and analytics.
• Exposure to Workday security configuration.

In return, you'll have the opportunity to influence change, develop your expertise and contribute to a transformation journey that is helping move Arriva forward.

Tempur Sealy is committed to improving the sleep of more people, every night, all around the world. As a leading designer, manufacturer, distributor, and retailer of bedding products worldwide, we know how crucial a good night of sleep is to overall health and wellness. Utilizing over a century of knowledge and industry-leading innovation, we deliver award-winning products that provide breakthrough sleep solutions to consumers in over 100 countries. Our highly recognized brands include Tempur-Pedic®, Sealy® and Stearns & Foster®. We hire people who have a passion for helping others find their best night’s sleep. No matter what stage of your career, you can build your future at Tempur Sealy!
Purpose of the role
The Tempur UK Transport team is a key part of the business. Their role is to liaise with and meet the needs of our customers. Tasks include making sure that all deliveries are made in a timely manner. Our customer base is varied and the team have to of manage both our retailer (over 200 retailers) and individual consumers. The team also need to liaise with our other operations departments and own stores.  This means that the team needs to be flexible and adaptable.
The Home Delivery Driver’s role is to make sure that all home deliveries go out in a timely manner, to make sure that we meet and exceed the expectations of our customers.  A good transport / deliveries service contributes considerably to our sales growth.
Key Responsibilities
• Deliver and install Tempur bed bases and mattresses.
• Carry out vehicle checks.
• Ensure that all the Company’s policies and administrative systems are properly adhered to so that the business runs smoothly.
• Work effectively as part of the Transport team.
• To be able to communicate effectively at all levels responding positively and within acceptable time scales to internal and external customer requests.
• Be able to overcome obstacles and adapt to the variance’s whilst being out on the road.
• Maintain all service levels and achieve targets.
• Ensure that all procedures within the department are adhered to and any changes to be notified to line manager.
• Ad hoc duties as and when required.
Knowledge/ Skills/ Experience/Profile
• The job holder should be an experienced delivery driver, with the ability to enter customers’ homes in the correct manner.
• The role will be 45 hours per week, Monday to Friday with varying start times from 6am. Finishing times will be once the days run has been completed regardless of hours worked.
Tempur Sealy International is committed to equal opportunities, and values diversity in our workforce. We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or any other legally protected characteristic. We maintain a fair and inclusive hiring process, ensuring that all candidates are evaluated based on their qualifications, skills, and experience. Our dedication to equal opportunities extends to every aspect of our organisation, fostering an inclusive and supportive work environment for all team members.
We are committed to the privacy and security of your personal data.  For more information on our practices, please see our applicant privacy policies available here.

Endless pre-loved items. A crucial source of fundraising. A store that runs your way.
Retail Store Manager
£27,336 - £32,067 per annum plus benefits
Reports to: Area manager
Department: ​Trading​
Contract: ​Permanent​
Hours: ​Full time 37.5 hours per week​
Location: St Annes
Closing date: 1st November 2026 23:55
Please note: You must be eligible to work in the UK to apply for this vacancy. Cancer Research UK is not able to offer visa sponsorship.
​​At Cancer Research UK, we exist to beat cancer.​
​​We are professionals with purpose, beating cancer every day. But we need to go much further and much faster. That’s why we’re looking for someone talented, someone who shares our vision, someone like you. ​
We’re looking for a motivating store manager to join Cancer Research UK’s trading team. You’ll be acting as an ambassador for Cancer Research UK, motivating your team to maximise on sales and fundraising targets. Your shop will be a place where your community gets to meet our people, understand our brand, and see some of the great things we do.
You’ll also be surrounded by people who are as dedicated to beating cancer as you are.
What will I be doing?
• Guiding, inspiring and engaging a team of paid staff and volunteers. This includes recruitment, retention and development of a diverse shop team.
• Taking ownership and responsibility for commercial running of your store including display and merchandising, stock management, maintaining shop standards, store layout, sales and income.
• Leading by example and providing excellent customer and supporter service.
• Maximising profit through effective cost control and sales.
• Creating relationships with your local community and Cancer Research UK colleagues.
• Organising and running creative fundraising events for your store to achieve fundraising targets.
• Maintaining compliance with health and safety, safeguarding, security, administration and HR policies.
• There will be a varied amount of manual handling and physical activity required within the day-to-day duties of the role.
What are you looking for?
• Experience of managing and inspiring a diverse team of people.
• Comfort working within targets and motivating others to achieve those targets.
• The ability to multi-task in a lively environment.
• Working knowledge of what makes great customer service.
• Commercial awareness.
• Knowledge of high street fashion retail.
• Adaptability in changing situations, including being able to work effectively independently.
• An awareness of the price, value and worth of items.
• Flexibility, our retail teams cover the needs of their stores by working on a rota basis. Whilst a level of flexibility is needed to meet the needs of the business, we don’t forget that you have a life outside of work too.
[Download the Candidate Pack]
What will I gain?
We make sure you are supported by a generous salary and benefits package, a wide range of career and personal development opportunities and high-quality tools, policies and processes to enable you to do your job well.
Our benefits package includes a substantial retirement plan, a generous and flexible leave allowance, discounts on anything from travel to technology, gym membership, and much more.
Our retail teams also have access to confidential wellbeing support from the Retail Trust.
How do I apply?
We operate an anonymised shortlisting process in our commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion. CVs are required for all applications; but we won’t be able to view them until we invite you for an interview. Instead, we ask you to complete the work history section of the online application form for us to be able to assess you quickly, fairly and objectively.
To support your training and development in this role, you will spend 4 weeks in a training shop, learning from a Training Shop Manager, this may be at a different location to the role you applied for.
Owing to the nature of this position, any offer of employment for this role will be subject to a satisfactory basic DBS check.
For more information on this career opportunity please visit our website or contact us at recruitment@cancer.org.uk.
For more updates on our work and careers, follow us on: Linked In, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.
Our vision is to create a charity where everyone feels like they belong, benefits from and participates in, the work we do. We actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and cultures, in particular those from ethnic minority backgrounds who are currently under-represented.
We want to see every candidate performing at their best throughout the job application process, interview process and whilst at work. We therefore ask you to inform us of any concerns you have or any adjustments you might need to enable this to happen. Please contact recruitment@cancer.org.uk or 020 3469 8400 as soon as possible.
Unfortunately, we are unable to recruit anyone below the age of 18, so that we can protect young people from health & safety and safeguarding risks.

Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely.
We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.
Summary:
Clio Operate, formally ShareDo, is a cutting-edge, adaptive work management platform that empowers large law firms to create customised solutions for managing their work processes. We focus on mid-sized to large law firms that use Clio Operate as their Case Management System to streamline operations, boost profitability, and enhance the client experience.
In March 2025, Clio — the global leader in cloud-based legal technology — announced the strategic acquisition of ShareDo. Headquartered in Vancouver, Canada, Clio also has offices in Toronto, Calgary, Dublin, Manchester, and Sydney with a global workforce of over 2000 employees.
Our Professional Services team will work with their team to get Clio Operate implemented and delivering value to their business. As part of that implementation lifecycle there will be Requirements workshops, playbacks, sprints, business change, user acceptance testing and
finally a hand-off to support.
We underpin that process with a bunch of different practices and processes; we are not wedded to a single methodology but rather to the mantra of continuous process improvement.
Depending upon the client initiative we are assisting with ShareDo implementations can be both big (10+ people in the project team) or small (part-time project team). At any one point we are running between 20 and 25 of these projects.
For our clients success looks like: quicker, more reliable, less costly implementations; easier business change and happy users; together with quicker realisation of business benefits .. simple!
For us success looks much the same with the addition of ensuring the professional services function delivers consistent profitability to the overall business.
The project management role is designed to ensure the successful implementation of ShareDo for both our clients and ourselves.
What you’ll work on:
•
Overall commercial accountability for a project
•
Resource management responsibility across a portfolio of projects
•
Working within the Service Delivery customer engagement process and driving continuous improvement
•
Managing finances, planning, risk and client stakeholders and relationships
•
Proactively managing and communicating with clients to ensure a high level of customer satisfaction
•
Collaborating with internal teams to maintain an ongoing understanding of features and functionality and translate the information into best practices for customers
What you may have:
•
Clearly, we’re looking for not just an experienced Project or Programme manager but some with a capability to deliver successful projects!
•
You’ll be strong on process, strong on change management, be a leader by example .. but a people person first and foremost.
•
Demonstrate a keen interest in improving your craft by using AI
•
You will be someone who relishes a challenge, someone who is driven by the satisfaction of creating something unique and of value.
•
You’re passionate about business change through technology and the possibilities that a product such as Clio Operate can bring to a business
•
You will be experienced in delivering projects and bringing them in on time and above customer expectations.
•
You will have attention to detail and have experience in project financial reporting.
•
You will have an understanding of SaaS architecture, modern software methodologies and the ability to communicate effectively with technical teams and understand the complexities of a product
•
You will have proven experience of managing projects using Agile methodologies and be capable of driving iterative delivery in a fast moving environment.
•
You will have excellent communication skills and be able to liaise between cross-functional teams, stakeholders and clients with the ability to translate technical concepts into language understandable to non-technical stakeholders.
•
You will have sharp analytical skills and be able to identify project risks, develop mitigation strategies and solve complex problems
•
Lastly, the experience and education question. Frankly, we’re slightly ambivalent. The number of years’ experience is irrelevant compared to the variety and relevance of that experience
What you will find here:
Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.
Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include:
•
Competitive, equitable salary
•
Clio offers a flexible hybrid work environment
•
25 days holiday + bank holidays
•
Private Healthcare with Life Insurance & Critical Illness cover
•
Pension contribution
•
Professional development and growth options
•
Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years
The expected salary range for this role is £64,900 to £87,900 GBP. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skillset, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile.
Diversity, Inclusion, Belonging and Equity (DIBE) & Accessibility
Our team shows up as their authentic selves, and are united by our mission. We are dedicated to diversity, equity and inclusion. We pride ourselves in building and fostering an environment where our teams feel included, valued, and enabled to do the best work of their careers, wherever they choose to log in from. We believe that different perspectives, skills, backgrounds, and experiences result in higher-performing teams and better innovation. We are committed to equal employment and we encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

AVEVA is creating software trusted by over 90% of leading industrial companies.
Job Title: Principal Technologist, Dev - AI Core Services Development
Location: Cambridge, UK
Employment Type: Regular, Full-Time (Hybrid)
We are looking for a hands-on Principal Engineer to join our Core AI Services team. In this role, you will help design, develop, and scale AI-enabling platform services and public APIs that are secure, reliable, and cloud-native. These services will act as foundational building blocks for AI adoption across AVEVA’s product portfolio and partner ecosystem.
Working at the forefront of agentic systems and harness engineering, you will join an agile Scrum team with a true builder mindset—delivering innovative, secure, and production-grade AI capabilities with the agility of a start-up. This role is ideal for an engineer with a genuine passion for keeping up with the latest AI engineering patterns and practices, eager to translate emerging tech into reliable, enterprise-ready software.
Key Responsibilities:
• Serve as the technical authority for core services owning design, reliability and performance.
• Build scalable, fault-tolerant cloud-native services on Microsoft Azure, ensuring high performance and reliability.
• Develop secure, well-documented public APIs and SDKs for consumption by internal and external developers.
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to deliver end-to-end solutions across data pipelines, orchestration, and service APIs.
• Embed robust security controls to protect sensitive data and ensure secure access to AI services.
• Lead and contribute to design reviews, code reviews, and architectural discussions to ensure engineering excellence.
• Mentor junior developers, encourage continuous learning, and contribute to a culture of innovation.
• Work with multiple teams to create AI solutions, which include AI model deployment, training, and AI tooling development.
Core Skills and Qualifications:
• 12+ years of experience in software engineering, preferably in platform or cloud-native service development using Microsoft and .NET technologies.
• Hands-on experience with containerised deployments in Kubernetes.
• Strong expertise in RESTful API design, versioning, testing, and lifecycle management.
• Proficient in securing APIs, managing authentication/authorization and data privacy practices.
• Fluent in developing code using AI Tools such as GitHub Copilot. Must be able to use prompt engineering to carry out multiple development tasks.
• Excellent problem-solving skills, with the ability to analyse complex technical challenges and propose scalable solutions.
• Experience working in Agile teams and collaborating across global R&D locations
• Demonstrated ability to mentor junior team members fostering a culture of continuous learning and innovation
Desirable Skills & Experience
• Familiarity with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), tool-calling, and AI orchestration frameworks (e.g., Semantic Kernel, Azure AI Foundry).
• Understanding of Large Language Models (LLMs) and the trade-offs between latency, capability, cost, and model sizing.
• Awareness of emerging AI protocols and standards (e.g., Model Context Protocol [MCP], Agent2Agent [A2A]).
• Exposure to automated AI evaluation, output benchmarking, and testing tools for AI-driven capabilities.
R&D at AVEVA
Our global team of 2000+ developers work on an incredibly diverse portfolio of over 75 industrial automation and engineering products, which cover everything from data management to 3D design. AI and cloud are at the centre of our strategy, and we have over 150 patents to our name.
UK Benefits include:
Flexible benefits fund, emergency leave days, adoption leave, 28 days annual leave (plus bank holidays), pension, life cover, private medical insurance, parental leave, education assistance program.
It’s possible we’re hiring for this position in multiple countries, in which case the above benefits apply to the primary location. Specific benefits vary by country, but our packages are similarly comprehensive.
Find out more: aveva.com/en/about/careers/benefits/
Hybrid working
We work in a hybrid way at AVEVA. Most roles are based at a local AVEVA office, with an expectation of being on-site 50% of your working hours to support collaboration and connection. Some positions are fully office-based depending on the nature of the work, and certain roles that support specific customers or markets may be remote. The working arrangement for this position will be confirmed during the hiring process.
Hiring process
Interested? Great! Get started by submitting your cover letter and CV through our application portal. AVEVA is committed to recruiting and retaining people with disabilities. Please let us know in advance if you need reasonable support during your application process.

AVEVA is a global leader in industrial software with more than 6,500 employees in over 40 countries. Our cutting-edge solutions are used by thousands of enterprises to deliver the essentials of life – such as energy, infrastructure, chemicals, and minerals – safely, efficiently, and more sustainably.

We're excited to be opening a brand-new Howdens depot and are looking for talented individuals to join us as an Apprentice from January 2027. Whether you're leaving school, college, or looking to take the first step in your career, we'll provide the training, support, and opportunities you need to succeed.

• Location: Skelmersdale Depot
• Salary: £16,686 plus team incentives

Learning and developing alongside experienced colleagues in a leading business to:

• Maintain high standards of safety and cleanliness
• Build relationships and support customers
• Developing confidence in a fast-paced depot environment
Who we’re looking for
• We hire for attitude and potential - not experience

Where this role can take you
• Warehouse Person

This apprenticeship is designed for individuals looking to develop new skills and begin or progress their career in this area. Ready to get started?
Apply today and take your first step with Howdens.

CRM Manager

About the Role & Team
Disney Destinations International (DDI) is seeking a CRM Manager to lead the delivery of audience-led CRM and email marketing programmes across Walt Disney World, Disneyland Paris and Disney Cruise Line throughout the UK & Ireland and wider EMEA markets.
Reporting to the Senior Marketing Manager, with a dotted reporting line to the Head of EMEA CRM, this role is responsible for developing and executing CRM strategies that drive engagement, guest lifetime value and commercial performance through best-in-class customer communications.
This role is based in our London Hammersmith office, with an expectation to work onsite four days per week.
Values
You’ll join a team grounded in our Disney values, acting with Integrity, welcoming everyone through Inclusion, embracing boundless Creativity, working together through Collaboration and caring deeply for our Community. These values shape how we work and how we support one another every day.
What You Will Do
• Develop and lead the annual EMEA CRM strategy across Walt Disney World, Disneyland Paris and Disney Cruise Line, aligning customer journeys and email communications to business objectives.
• Build, manage and optimise email campaigns and automated journeys within Salesforce Marketing Cloud, ensuring brand excellence, accuracy and strong customer experience.
• Deliver end-to-end CRM campaign planning, including annual, monthly and weekly calendars, audience targeting, creative development, testing and deployment.
• Work with internal stakeholders and external agencies to brief, develop and deliver CRM creative assets and campaigns.
• Collaborate with EMEA CRM, Data & Analytics and Deployment teams to ensure campaigns are data-led, measurable and commercially effective.
• Analyse campaign performance, establish KPIs and implement test-and-learn programmes to improve engagement, conversion, deliverability and revenue contribution.
• Develop audience segmentation and targeting strategies using customer insights and behavioural data.
• Ensure all CRM activity complies with GDPR, privacy regulations and internal governance standards.
• Manage CRM budgets, vendor relationships, purchase orders and reconciliation activities.
• Present performance updates, insights and strategic recommendations to senior stakeholders and leadership teams.
Required Qualifications & Skills

Company:
Oliver Wyman
Description:
Who we are
Oliver Wyman is a global management consulting firm. We work with clients through their most defining moments, combining deep industry knowledge, specialized expertise, and the power of perspective to help them adapt, grow, and thrive.
We believe diverse perspectives make the work stronger. Our consultants bring different backgrounds, experiences, and ways of thinking to help solve complex problems and create lasting impact for clients, colleagues, and communities.
At Oliver Wyman, we are proud of the values that we aspire to live by. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and reach their full potential.
Quotient — AI by Oliver Wyman brings together deep industry insight, strategic advisory, and hands-on AI delivery to help organizations move from proof to production and from production to enterprise value.
The role
WAVE is a newly created team within Quotient. It exists to accelerate AI-enabled business development and help our teams move faster, think differently, and build with reuse in mind.
As Platform / Infrastructure Engineer, you will own the foundations that make WAVE work. You will design and maintain the infrastructure that allows a small, fast-moving team to prototype quickly, deploy reliably, and scale with confidence. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys building dependable engineering foundations and creating self-serve platforms that help others move faster.
What you will do
You will create the infrastructure that lets WAVE move from idea to deployment with speed, consistency, and control.
You will:
•
Design, build, and maintain the team’s cloud infrastructure and deployment pipelines.
•
Set up CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, and disaster-recovery capabilities so solutions can move from prototype to deployment quickly and repeatably.
•
Provide infrastructure as a service to the rest of the team through self-serve environments that do not bottleneck on you.
•
Advise on the right infrastructure setup for each solution, including what is needed to support scale.
•
Work closely with the AI Engineers to ensure their work can be deployed, monitored, and maintained effectively.
•
Help WAVE make practical choices about environment design, release management, and operational resilience.
•
Support a consistent engineering experience across projects, so the team can build once and reuse where possible.
•
Contribute to a platform mindset across WAVE, where infrastructure is treated as a product the team can rely on.
How you will be measured
Our success is simple to state: the team should be able to move fast without losing reliability. You’ll know you are succeeding when engineers can self-serve the environments they need, when deployments are smooth and repeatable, and when the infrastructure consistently supports a growing pipeline of reusable AI work.
Why join us?
You can be your best here. At Oliver Wyman, you will find meaningful work, talented people, and a culture built on trust, support, and growth.
Create solutions that have impact
•
Build the technical foundations that help WAVE deliver AI-enabled work faster and more reliably.
•
Help turn promising ideas into deployable solutions that can support proposals, prototypes, and reusable assets.
•
Be part of a team where your work directly shapes what the business can build, reuse, and scale.
Develop as a leader
•
Take ownership from day one in a role that sits at the centre of WAVE’s engineering environment.
•
Build credibility by helping others move quickly without compromising quality, reliability, or good engineering practice.
•
Lead through technical judgement, practical problem solving, and clear communication.
Learn without limits
•
Build a rare mix of cloud engineering, platform thinking, and exposure to AI-enabled consulting work.
•
Work closely with AI Engineers, the Technical Business Partner, and colleagues across Quotient and the wider firm.
•
Deepen your understanding of how to design infrastructure for speed, reuse, and scale in a consulting environment.
Thrive in a vibrant and inclusive culture
•
Work as part of a collaborative team that values different perspectives and practical problem solving.
•
Help shape how a new team grows, in a culture where people are encouraged to speak up, share ideas, and move quickly together.
•
Join an environment that supports inclusion, teamwork, and mutual respect.
Experience rewards that work for you
•
Enjoy a role designed for learning, visibility, and growth inside a newly created team.
•
Be part of a pilot that is built to scale, giving you exposure to how a new capability is shaped from the ground up.
•
Work in a way that supports performance, development, and sustainability.
Who can apply?
We are looking for someone who is comfortable building and running internal platforms that other engineers depend on. The right person will combine strong engineering depth with practical judgement, and will enjoy working in a small team where infrastructure directly shapes delivery speed and quality.
This role is well suited to someone who wants to work at the intersection of cloud engineering, platform reliability, and AI-enabled delivery.
Required qualifications
•
Strong hands-on experience with Kubernetes and a major cloud platform, ideally Azure and/or AWS.
•
Solid experience with CI/CD and infrastructure-as-code.
•
Experience designing and supporting disaster-recovery capabilities.
•
Ability to build and run internal platforms that other engineers depend on.
•
Practical understanding of how to support deployment, reliability, and scale across multiple solutions.
•
Full professional English.
Preferred qualifications
•
Experience supporting data and AI workloads in production.
•
Familiarity with Polaris
•
Experience working in a fast-moving environment with multiple concurrent initiatives.
•
Experience shaping platform standards or reusable engineering patterns.
How to apply
Please submit your CV and cover letter. If shortlisted, you will be invited to meet members of the WAVE team and discuss your experience, motivation, and approach to the role.
What to expect during the interview process
At Oliver Wyman, we want you to shine in your interview. Our process is designed like our work environment — it is challenging, exciting, and fun.
We keep our process short and transparent:
• Screening conversation with the team lead.
• Technical exercise relevant to the role, either take-home or live depending on the stage.
• Two to three team-fit and craft interviews, including at least one with a partner.
• Offer.
We assess both technical craft and the ability to work fluidly with a multidisciplinary team.

When our values align, there's no limit to what we can achieve.
At Parexel, we all share the same goal - to improve the world's health. From clinical trials to regulatory, consulting, and market access, every clinical development solution we provide is underpinned by something special - a deep conviction in what we do.
Each of us, no matter what we do at Parexel, contributes to the development of a therapy that ultimately will benefit a patient. We take our work personally, we do it with empathy and we're committed to making a difference.
Parexel is in the business of improving the world’s health. We do this by providing a suite of biopharmaceutical services that help clients across the globe transform scientific discoveries into new treatments. From clinical trials to regulatory, consulting, and market access, our therapeutic, technical, and functional ability is underpinned by a deep conviction in what we do. We believe in our values, Patients First, Quality, Respect, Empowerment & Accountability.
We are currently recruiting for Clinical Research Associate II and Senior Clinical Research Associate to join our Multi-Sponsor Clinical Trials Team in the UK.
This role if fully decentralised in the UK.
Your time here
At Parexel, the CRA role offers the opportunity to go beyond the role of a typical clinical monitor. CRA’s are accountable for using their expertise to build and maintain the site relationship and ensure they’re set up for success. As the clinical sites’ sole point of contact, this includes addressing and resolving site issues and questions. You’ll also manage site quality and delivery from site identification through to close-out.
As a CRA, Parexel will offer you world class technology and training catered to your individual experience. You can anticipate less travel and a lower protocol load in comparison to industry peers. Your hard work may be rewarded through a bonus incentive program, the opportunity to work within multiple therapeutic areas and an opportunity to advance your career in clinical research. If impact, flexibility, and career development appeal to you, Parexel could be your next home.
What you’ll do
• Leverage your expertise. Conduct qualification visits (QV), site initiation visits (SIV), monitoring visits (MV) and termination visits (TV) at assigned clinical sites and generate visit/contact reports.
• Build relationships. Oversee integrity of the study and utilize problem-solving skills to promote rapport with the site and staff.
• Protect patients. Review the performance of the trial at designated sites, ensure the rights and well-being of human subjects are safeguarded and are in accordance with protocol.
• Drive productivity. Develop patient recruitment strategies in conjunction with the clinical site to meet enrollment timelines, while also ensuring compliance with the approved standard operating procedures (SOPs), protocol/amendment(s), GCP, and the applicable regulatory requirement(s).
• Ensure quality. Evaluate the quality and integrity of the reported data, site efficacy and drug accountability.
• Execute. Monitor the completeness and quality of Regulatory Documentation and perform site document verification.
More about you
On your first day we’ll expect you to have:
• Site Management or equivalent experience in clinical research, with understanding of clinical trials methodology and terminology.
• Ability to perform all clinical monitoring activities independently.
• Bachelor’s or equivalent degree in biological science, pharmacy or other health related discipline.
• Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills within a matrixed team.
• Experience working in a self-driven capacity, with a sense of urgency and limited oversight.
• A client-focused approach to work and flexible attitude with respect to assignments/new learning.
• The ability to manage multiple tasks, evaluate a variety of unpredictable scenarios and achieve project timelines while being able to apply your understanding of study protocol(s).
• An honest and ethical work approach to promote the development of life changing treatments for patients.
• Strong computer skills, including but not limited to the knowledge of a Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS), Electronic Document Management System (EDMS) and MS-Office products such as Excel and Word.
If you are ready to join Parexel’s Journey, please apply!
